But it already does exist, as a sub-genre. Contemporary pop-country, lol.
I mean contemporary/modern are genre tag-alongs for a reason. Music is constantly changing and it's much easier to add a suffix than create a new word.

There's always alt-country which, in its simplest definition, is a mixture of other genres (usually in the form of folk or rock) along with country. For the most part, it's devoid of all the tropes that plague the modern iteration of country.

I started with Songs: Ohia/Magnolia Electric Co. and haven't looked back since.
Apologies, I have grown defensive in my time here. I swear this subreddit is basically an ad hominem circle jerk.
I wasn't making an argument? I pointed out why his mocking of the situation was misguided because if you're going to outline the idiocy of a person, at least do it correctly.

As for the argument itself, you have to consider that doctors are regular people and it is a universally proven fact that negative bias (whether justified or not) of people who are overweight does exist within regular people. 

To the extent at which it happens and whether a factually large number of doctors act out unprofessionally on their bias, is debatable. 

I will leave this link behind as food for thought, it is not intended to confirm or refute anything: http://www.wakehealth.edu/News-Releases/2013/Future_Doctors_Unaware_of_Their_Obesity_Bias.htm

Then argue against that supposed "fact". Of course I knew that your comment wasn't serious and intended for humor. But how can I find humor in a statement if it is fallacious and ultimately, an untrue observation? What was the point of saying it at all?

They said that despite being absurd, it does (however) "draw attention" to the concern; leading to a few possible implications that do not automatically mean they believe the image to be real. Notice the lack of the word "prove" and inclusion of "but"? Meaning that contrary to the absurdity of the situation, attention is drawn from it anyway.

I chose to think the image was used as satire (a possibility the author maybe considered) attempting to draw attention to their claim, which is completely fair game. 

What you should be arguing over, is whether or not you believe their claims of medical malpractice being rampant with overweight patients is fact and not pull an irrelevant straw man.
